unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U07: Identify goods,price,delivery and documents of title

payload.title: Classify the asset and the transfer
payload.core_explanation_md:
The Sale of Goods framework concerns the stated movable property category, including shares and things agreed to be severed, but excluding money and actionable claims as goods. Price is money consideration; barter and an immovable-property transfer need a different legal analysis. General contract essentials still apply.

Delivery transfers possession, which need not be the same event as passing ownership. A document of title can support possession/control in the described commercial framework; not every invoice or certificate has that legal character. Specific goods are identified at contracting, while future goods are to be produced or acquired later. Verify what exists and what right the document actually conveys.

self_check.prompt_text: Does a seller invoice automatically become a document of title?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. The legal character and commercial control function must be established.

payload.stem_md: A lending file treats every commercial invoice as a document of title giving control of stored goods. What is needed?

options.text_md: Examine the document legal character and actual possession/control effect
options.explanation_md: An invoice label alone does not establish title-document status.
Length is irrelevant to the right conveyed.

options.text_md: Assume all documents transfer ownership and possession identically
options.explanation_md: Different documents and events have distinct effects.
The relevant goods must still be established.

payload.correct_explanation_md: An invoice label alone does not establish title-document status.

payload.stem_md: A seller promises goods it will manufacture later. Which distinction is material?

options.text_md: They are necessarily identified existing goods merely because a price is agreed
options.explanation_md: Price does not make future goods existing.

options.text_md: No contract can ever concern future goods
Future goods differ from goods already specifically identified at the contract date
options.explanation_md: Timing and identification matter to the transaction.

options.text_md: The buyer automatically owns every asset of the seller
options.explanation_md: The promise does not create that broad ownership.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Timing and identification matter to the transaction.
